Added and committed two regression tests covering the declaration load failures:

- A child declaration with an explicit ultimate payer loads without incorrectly requiring a selected parent payer.
- A company number stays paired with the `Company` donor kind when funder observations are grouped.

Both tests pass. Each also failed when I temporarily restored its original bug, confirming they catch the regressions. Formatting passed, and I updated [PR #26](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/26) with the test results.

The changes are committed on `fix/declaration-loader-parent-basis-20261008` as `c3640b0`. The local `todo.md` remains uncommitted. This follows the root-cause and behavior-focused testing principles: the tests exercise the loader’s observable results and demonstrate that each original failure is detected.

The resolver keeps both organizations separate when the evidence doesn’t meet its merge rules. Search then ranks each stored funder record independently, so it can show several related names together.

- **HSBC:** The two bank names differ only in capitalization and normalize to the same name. One pair with the same normalized address was merged. Another pair had a comma difference in the stored address, which the resolver treated as an address disagreement and rejected. The CEO-named record has a different name and role; its match remained in review. Its reported company number, `9928412`, is seven characters, so it doesn’t qualify as a company identity anchor. These decisions appear in the [local run’s pair decisions](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/data/01a11ac3-40f7-765f-8040-33e2c918a342/resolved/declarations/pair_decisions.parquet). The [resolver rules](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/domain/models/declaration_resolution/identity.rs:72) require stronger evidence across roles, and require company numbers to be eight characters [to use as an anchor](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/domain/models/declaration_resolution/identity.rs:38).

- **Unite:** Names such as `Unite`, `Unite Union`, and `Unite the Union` are not exact normalized matches, so they don’t qualify for the resolver’s exact-name donor rule. For example, `Unite Union` and `Unite` share a donor role and address, but their pair was left in review because their names differ. Regional entries also have different recorded addresses; some comparisons were rejected on that basis. The [local pair decisions](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/data/01a11ac3-40f7-765f-8040-33e2c918a342/resolved/declarations/pair_decisions.parquet) show these outcomes. The written [resolution policy](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/docs/funder-resolution-design.md:45) explicitly leaves fuzzy-name and alias matches without an automatic merge rule.

The search query returns qualifying funder rows by name or alias and rank; it doesn’t combine similar rows at display time ([search query](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/outbound/funder.rs:22)). The loader creates records from the resolver’s identity groups ([loader](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/outbound/declaration_loading.rs:394)).

One test is easy to misread: `shows_no_hsbc_duplicates` checks that each exact HSBC spelling appears once. It still expects the three spellings as separate results; it does not verify that they resolve to one HSBC identity ([test](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/tests/integration.rs:30)).

Whether Unite’s regional offices and Parliamentary Staff Branch should be merged under one parent identity is still an open domain decision; the data alone doesn’t establish that. I found no HSBC-specific deduplication ticket or relevant Google Drive document.

as far as i'm concerned, the deduplication work is far from complete. If we can't resolve those two differently spelled HSBC records or most of the unite unions then our pipeline is not working. We did a LOT of component extraction in the cleaning. What purpose does this serve?

content.text:
The user’s criticism is supported by the implementation: most cleaning features currently serve as retained evidence for future resolution, and do not affect present deduplication.

The cleaner derives punctuation-normalized tokens, sorted token keys, organisation cores, person cores and initials, explicit aliases, validated acronyms and expansions, and parenthetical evidence in [funder_name.rs](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-declaration-loader-fix-20261008/exposed/src/lib/domain/models/funder_name.rs:20). It writes them to the cleaned Parquet schema in [declaration_cleaning.rs](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-declaration-loader-fix-20261008/exposed/src/lib/outbound/declaration_cleaning.rs:296). Their purpose is sensible: retain original evidence alongside several representations so matching can distinguish cosmetic variation, legal suffixes, trading names, acronyms, and contextual text without destroying source information.

But the resolver deserializes the Parquet rows into `Observation`, which has **only `name_normalized` as its name feature**, plus normalized address, kind, company number, role and provenance. The other columns are ignored by serde. See [input.rs](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-declaration-loader-fix-20261008/exposed/src/lib/domain/models/declaration_resolution/input.rs:10) and the read in [declaration_resolution.rs](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-declaration-loader-fix-20261008/exposed/src/lib/outbound/declaration_resolution.rs:40). Its scorer request narrows this further to name, address and candidate eligibility ([ComparisonRow](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-declaration-loader-fix-20261008/exposed/src/lib/domain/models/declaration_resolution/input.rs:192)).

Splink scores exact full names, edit distance ≤2, and exact addresses; it has no organisation-core/token/alias/acronym comparisons ([model.json](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-declaration-loader-fix-20261008/resolution/exposed_resolution/model.json:18)). More decisively, Rust requires **exact normalized full-name equality even for the statistical automatic merge**. A fuzzy-name pair cannot merge through that rule regardless of its score ([identity.rs](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-declaration-loader-fix-20261008/exposed/src/lib/domain/models/declaration_resolution/identity.rs:76)). It additionally accepts exact names for donor/donor pairs without the address/score threshold. Company-number equality is a separate seed mechanism.

Thus:
- HSBC PLC/plc case normalization is already consumed and should yield identical normalized names; the unresolved observation must be explained through roles/address/published-run state, rather than missing case handling.
- Unite punctuation/token variations and organisation-name variants cannot benefit from the rich cleaning output today.
- These features are not wasted extraction, but their connection to matching is unfinished. Saying “the policy leaves them for review” describes the gap; it does not demonstrate successful deduplication.

Also, the loader’s `aliases` are distinct `name_raw` values inside an already resolved group, **not the cleaner’s `explicit_aliases`** ([declaration_loading.rs](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-declaration-loader-fix-20261008/exposed/src/lib/outbound/declaration_loading.rs:406)). Extracted trading aliases are not automatically exposed as database search aliases either.

The docs explicitly call these “independent candidates for future resolution” ([declaration-cleaning.md](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-declaration-loader-fix-20261008/docs/declaration-cleaning.md:65)). That establishes the intended staging but confirms the current pipeline hasn’t completed the next stage. No edits made.
